review_highlights.comment: One of the most engaging lecturers I have had. His class is very interesting and builds on itself in a way that makes sense. Quizzes are difficult and typically had averages of 50-60s. Exams have a lot of content but as long as you start early they are pretty straightforward. Very test heavy grading but does give extra credit for participation.

Very interesting class but the only way to do well on exams is to get the back exams from the union. He isn't very accessible outside of class and overall, the course structure was disorganized. He would often not give directions for bigger projects until the last minute.

Interesting class. Exams were difficult but very close to back exams from the union. Assignments in the syllabus were mentioned but specific instructions were not given to us until very close to the deadline. He will cold call and grill your responses. Nice and willing to reschedule quizzes and exams. Just a lot of disorganization.

He was a great lecturer with understandable slides. The exams were fair but you definitely needed to study a lot for them. We had extra credit but you need a 95 for an A. TA review sessions were extremely helpful and Rojas was helpful in office hours. Grades took a long time to be put into LMS but overall biomaterials is a good course- just study!

Dr. Rojas is a good professor. Not a lot of homework. Definitely cares about his students and is very approachable. He rushes through lectures but the slide material is good and easy to review. He is sometimes unclear about content for assignments/quizzes. Tests were difficult but awesome TA review sessions and forgiving grading helped a ton.

analysis.name: Mohammad   Amiri
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Absolute worst professor in the history of RPI professors. After the final, I walked through the hood in the middle of the road and unfortunately did not get hit. Cant put into words how horrible this class is, makes a math lover hate math.

Amiri has a teaching problem, that is he cannot teach at all. His ability to lecture solely depends on if you understand the concept the first time he explains it. His teaching methods are incredibly notation-heavy, but he will never post his notes (so be ready to write down everything). No prep content for exams either. Just use the textbook.

Being smart and being a good teacher aren't always the same. Amiri makes some effort to connect with students, but he is meant to teach grad students. He is too smart to teach such an important undergrad class. I really think he cares, he encourages questions and gets excited when they are asked, but I think he should stick to grads and research

Trying to follow along during lectures is a nightmare. His explanations along with his notes are unhelpful at best, as everything is exclusively written with utmost mathematical formality and notation, making it incredibly difficult to understand being new to this material. I'd say more but there's a word cap. RPI needs to reevaluate this course.

Class slides are abhorent as the material is delivered in a graduate-level research style for what should be a sophomore class. Lectures are formatted poorly with random pop quizzes and no structure. He creates irrelevant homework with AI that's more difficult than the exams. You are better off taking an actual math class.

He is amazing and genuinely a caring kind professor w/ dad jokes.

--took 2340--
Excellent professor. Very kind and honest, earned a ton from him-- he takes this job more like coaching for success and it works really well. Not too hard, and a very enjoyable class. 10/10 would take again, he's one of my favorite professors here.
He is a really good teacher, one of the best classes I took. It helped me a lot with my public speaking skills.

Prof Hiland is my favorite professor at this school. I took Intro to Comm Theory and Speech Communication with him.  He is first of all very knowledgeable on the subjects but is also really open to discussing and debating with students. He makes sure that his students are actually learning, and every assignment is useful. 100% recommend.

He insists we call him "AL," and he's the funniest dude at RPI. His lectures are good for Public Speaking, and he will actually help you become a better speaker if you put in the effort. review_highlights.comment: Intro to Engineering is an easy class if you show up to lecture and pay even somewhat attention. He is pretty clear in explaining things, though FYI he does have an accent. Do the back tests and you'll be fine.

I took Shahsavari for engineering dynamics.  The lectures are not mandatory, however the tests pull from the in class examples along with the optional homework.  If you do the examples in class along with the homework as well, you will get A's on the tests.  If you go to office hours and get to know him, he is helpful in more ways than one.

Second time having Prof. Shahsavari. Lecture notes are useful but it is boring to watch him write everything out in class. Tests are difficult but everything was given a generous curve. He is concerned with student performance and encourages people to come to office hours, which I have found more useful than class itself.

Strength of Materials is a tough class. Examples he presents are helpful studying for tests and doing hw. Has slight accent but doesn't adversely affect presentation. Very willing to help during office hours and is concerned with each student's performance. Would recommend.

Prof Shahsavari was pretty accessible during the MSL in-class lab but whenever my team asked a question, he often responded pretty vaguely and didn't really help identify the problem. However, he kept the class timely and we always finished on time.

review_highlights.comment: Not good at teaching the content - assumes you know things that are not taught in the prereq courses. His exam questions do not match the lectures. For some reason the class is 95 A and Gittens made multiple errors on a HW problem during office hours. Then he had the audacity to use ChatGPT to solve the problem for him. Apparently, the questions were made by DiTursi and not him, but he did not understand the content at all. He reads of Malik's slides, but doesn't get what is going on in them.

The lectures consist of the Gittens rewriting a few lines from each chapter of the textbook, verbatim. His lectures offer no explanation beyond these few words. Too, gittens does not work through any examples. It is clear Gittens did not come to RPI as a professor and cares little for the students, rather came for research and is forced to teach

Heavy Homework. 
But it is so easy to lose points on multiple choice questions on quiz and exam. 
There are 13 homework and takes several hours every week. 
Homework will not never stop, especially there will be a homework deadline on you quiz and exam day.

The homeworks were super easy and I very much enjoyed doing them. The lectures were super informative and helpful. review_highlights.comment: Very good, Prof. She is really understandable and outgoing. The class requires a bit of reading and writing but worth it because she grades very nicely and if not she'll explain really cleary why.

intro to cog neur -- awesome instructor, passionate about the subject/her research, straightforward assignments/exams, quiz every lecture based on prev lecture, patient and thorough answering questions. would recommend this professor.
Had for inquiry CCWB, not psych. Professor Walf was very kind and caring, and genuinely wants students to succeed. Gives good feedback on essays, and workload was very manageable.

Had Dr. Walf for INQR 1175, not PSYC 1200. Very kind professor, enjoyed participating in her class discussions and the classwork was very doable. Literally went to class the first day, finished all the homework's the first week, took the exams throughout the sem and got an a in the class. review_highlights.comment: His lecture style of presenting concepts and equations then applying them to example textbook problems worked very well. There were pop quizzes throughout the semester but they were straightforward and graded leniently. Great professor!

The semester started rough, but the professor was open to criticism and feedback and made positive changes to the way the class was operating. He was very willing to review exams and offer valuable advice on how to study. Most importantly, he was flexible with exam makeups, which a lot of RPI professors do not usually allow. Great class experience!

Great prof, lectures were great, starting with a few derivations and moves onto examples afterwards. There is optional homework assigned every lecture with the solution posted with it to help one study, in class quizzes occasionally, exams were fair and if you studied the homework and examples, you would surely do well.

Great Professor. This was his first year teaching, but he crushed it! Very available outside of class time for extra help, and is readily available if you need concepts in class explained beyond what is covered in class. Tests are challenging but fair, and are very representative of the (optional) homework material given.

Dr. Amjad was a great professor throughout the whole semester. His first few days started off kind of rocky, but after that he rocketed to being the best professor of the semester. His Dynamics class was honestly very enjoyable, not to mention that Dr. Amjad himself is a great person and wants you to succeed. 10/10.

analysis.name: Arshad Chowdhury
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Lectures maybe a bit long at times but if you follow through it is very simple. Since this class rely a lot on consulting to empirically found curves and graphs, and his lecture slides have clear pipeline on how to approach a problem, the exams are very straightforward. Also his homeworks are CONSIDERABLY harder than exam which is super helpful.

Good professor overall. The class was pretty large and there weren't attendance or quiz points, so your grade mainly depends on the exams. He covered a lot of material in a short time, and most of it was explained clearly. You just have to keep up on your own since everything moves fast.

Dr. Chowdhury is a really good professor. He gets how students think, which makes his class way easier to follow. The way he organizes stuff and keeps a good pace during lectures is super helpful. Plus, he does a ton of example problems in class, which makes it way easier to understand everything. Exams are open book and notes and pretty fair.

Great professor! Super understanding and supportive, especially during a summer course when things are rushed. His lecture videos were short, clear, and straight to the point, which made the material easy to follow without feeling overwhelming. Very organized and really cares about his student's success.

Professor was okay, nothing really stood out to me. The exams felt really long and hard to finish, but he does grade pretty leniently. The course overall was tough for me, and I think the material could've been organized better.

analysis.name: Sibel Adali
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 50 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: One of the better CS profs. Looking at older comments, I get the idea she's come a long way. She really knows her stuff and puts a lot of work into the class. She is very nice and helpful in office hours. The class is challenging, but fair, and certainly not impossible. The average on exam 1 was 83, exam 2: 85, final: 77.
She's one of the nicest and funniest professors. CS1 with her was an easy A for someone with no prior experience.

Despite getting a relatively low grade in the class, I really feel like I learned the topic. DBS is pretty comprehensive and Dr Adali seems like she's made an effort to seriously streamline the course so that exams and homework test your knowledge of the topics rather than act as busywork. Strongly reccomend.

Great professor! Class easy as long as you attend lectures and take notes. Super helpful and knowledgeable. Highly recommend - teaches topics for real-life applications (job interviews, etc.). As long as you put in effort, you will do good.

She's very engaging and uses good example problems to keep students interested. Gives three late days for no points off during the semester. Homework and labs can be really tricky, there're frequently lots of kids in office hours the day before an assignment is due, but they are graded generously. Hw grade counteracts my low (70's) test average.

analysis.name: Belmiro Galo
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 69 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Funny. Caring. Understanding. Probably the best professor at RPI. Dude rocks. It is clear he wants his students to success in his class, and goes out of his way to help. Math in general is a hard subject to sit through a whole lecture for, but Professor Belmiro makes it fun. Cannot recommend him enough, I genuinely do not have anything bad to say.

Dr. Galo is an A- professor . His classes are engaging and even fun, which isn't always easy with tough subjects like Diffeq & Multi. I took both with him, and while the exams are definitely challenging, they're kind of fair and cover all material well. If you put in the effort, you'll learn a lot. He also offers a lot of EC if the average is bad

Had him for Intro to Diff Eq, first time for him and me. Funny and a decent lecturer, but quite theory heavy over intuitive/practical apps. Rec's always curveballs, TAs run them independently. Low exam avgs b/c he thought we were juniors w/ multivar and linalg instead of 1st/2nd-years w/ calc2, but gives EC assignments to compensate exam avg to 75.

Calc 2 with him was a pretty good class overall. He explains the theory behind processes, not just application, which can be good or bad depending on how you learn. I enjoyed most lectures, but his tests are quite challenging. If averages are low, he gives EC to boost everyone. He's also a nice guy to talk to in and out of class.

One of the best professors I've had at RPI. Made multi extremely understandable and bridged into lin alg well. Offered extra credit assignments when exam grades got low, very caring about his students and their grades. Also, one of the funniest guys I've ever met. Great professor overall.

analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He is understandable and draws excellent diagrams during lectures which really help visualize the concepts and problems covered. The class and exam structure makes it difficult to do well, and although he is not very entertaining or engaging during his lectures, he is a solid professor and will teach you the material if you don't fall asleep.

Yes, I failed the class. But I recognize that it is only the fault of my own. He's the best you can get for IEA, and he has office hours for a very long time. MAKE USE OF THAT! It will be easy to fall behind in this class because of its very fast pace, but if you work hard, you'll do well. His lectures are clear and thorough.

Could not ask for a better professor. As long as you put in some effort into this class, you'll do fine. He is insanely good at explaining material so MAKE SURE TO GO TO LECTURES, especially since there are in-class assignments. Professor Tathagata makes difficult concepts easy to grasp. An amazing professor who genuinely cares for his students.

Prof. Bhaduri is a great professor, who gave interesting lectures. Strength of Materials was very, very, hard, but he did try his best to help, and the materials posted on LMS were invaluable for my final.
Also, was very understanding when I had to miss a test, which was very nice as things were very awful that week for me.

He's a real nice prof - lectures are well-structured, and his explanations are in-depth. Despite the difficulty of the class, he is very encouraging and helpful; he seems to genuinely want his students to succeed.

Good teacher don't know why he gets so much hate, it's people venting their incompetence in thermo.

Theo is late and never prepared for class. He insists on doing ICAs that take half of the class time and are not relevant to future homeworks or exams. The way he designed Heat Transfer is not conducive of learning.

Boring lectures. Reads off the slides and is difficult to understand. Slides are copied from the textbook and he doesnt elaborate on any concepts in class very well. Reading the textbook is crucial for success.

I don't get why his ratings are so low on here. His lectures can definitely get boring especially because they're at 8 am, but he's incredibly knowledgeable on thermo. There are no exams/quizzes, only homework and a final course project.

Professors Bram and Milanese are so kind. I would be happy to have them again but did not enjoy the class in a content perspective. I thought it would be technology impacts on the world but it's a philosophy/critical thinking class. If you enjoy that I recommend the class, it just isn't my cup of tea. Class was also 5 assignments, all groupwork.

Had Bram for both IFL and critical thinking. Overall engaging lecturer for two interesting and complementary classes. Logic is very challenging, proof related homeworks took me about 10 hours a week and 40% of your grade is distributed between just four 3-6 question quizzes. Would, however, still recommend him for it over Bringsjord.

Great class with a knowledgeable teacher. The assignments were challenging and there were only 6 major ones, so your grade felt really dependent on those. A lot of the work was group-based. Despite that, I appreciate how the course sparked my interest in Cognitive Science, and I'm considering it for my focus.
Bram is a funny guy and a great professor. His lecture slides can tend to get a bit boring, however his energy and jokes make up for it.

Was significantly more a problem in multi for me, matrix it was really helpful how clear she was. Would take again for sure.

She is very strict and not very lenient for students. Don't ask her to round anything up, for extra credit, or any other help with conflicts with classes. She will just claim that since her class has no final it's more important. It's cause of her strictness is why I did poor in her class.

Took this class fall-25 (my first semester). It was great being able to not show up on Friday mornings. There are 4 tests (no final) and 10 ish quizzes which is kinda a lot but overall she's a good lecturer and easy class.
Her lectures are amazing and if you miss class her notes are still easily understandable. She is a very strict grader and fairly uncompromising on any conflicts you may have.
